title: compile.ts: bake motion guide path into published SWF PlaceObject2 transforms
description:
compile.ts calls getTweenedFrame(layer, frameIdx) at lines 957 and 981 WITHOUT passing the timeline argument. The getTweenedFrame signature is getTweenedFrame(layer, frameIndex, timeline?) — the third param is required for guide-layer path following. Without it, guided-layer objects interpolate linearly between their start/end keyframe positions in the published SWF instead of following the guide path.

The canvas preview is CORRECT: packages/core/src/engine/snapshot.ts line 40 calls getTweenedFrame(layer, frameIndex, scene.timeline) and correctly produces path-following positions.

Fix: In the frame loop in compile.ts (around line 957), pass the current scene's timeline as the third argument. The variable 'scene' (doc.scenes[sceneIdx]) is already in scope, and scene.timeline is available. After the fix, for each frame of a guided layer, getTweenedFrame will call samplePath() + getGuideLayerPath() (in packages/core/src/engine/guidepath.ts) and return the path-sampled x/y (and rotation if motionOrientToPath=true) rather than the naive linear interpolation.

Acceptance: add an e2e test in apps/desktop/e2e/visual-oracle.spec.ts (or a new motion-guide.spec.ts) that authors a guide layer with a curved path, a guided layer with a motion tween, publishes a SWF, plays it in Ruffle, and screenshots at frame N to confirm the object is positioned on the curve rather than on the straight-line midpoint.
